(Exparte)
 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
Sriram .B.V vs Prakash .K.K on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141727136/
1
On 06.12.2021 at about 8.00 a.m., petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-ET-7924 near Doddamage village Koratikere Cross, Doddamage Hobli, Arakalagudu Taluk, Hassan District.
At that time a Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3170 came in rash and negligent manner and has dashed against him.
Due to the impact of a accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

3. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Arakalagudu wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Government Hospital, Hassan and then to Janapriya Hospital Hassan wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The x-ray report revealed that he had comminuted fracture of Pelvic injury with fracture of acetabulum right with sutured wound right knee.
He has advice for regular dressing, physiotherapy and follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 46 years as on the date of accident.
He was a agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.

6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent drive of the respondent No.1, who drove his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3170.
7.
The respondent is the owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till the realization.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
8. After registration of the petition, notice was issued against respondent.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent, the respondent is placed exparte.
9. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
In addition to his evidence, the petitioner got examined the doctor, who has issued disability certificate for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
11.

Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following points:
Sriram .B.V vs Prakash .K.K on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141727136/
2 1.

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner prove that, he has sustained grievous in- juries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.13- C-3170 by its driver, in RTA took place on 06.12.2021 at about 8.00 a.m., on Doddamage Village, Koratikere Cross,
Doddamage Hobli, Arakalagudu Taluk, Hassan District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
12. My findings on the above points are as under.

Point No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Point No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Point No.3 : As per the final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
13.

The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 06.12.2021 at about 8.00 a.m., petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-ET-7924 near Doddamage village Koratikere Cross, Doddamage Hobli, Arakalagudu Taluk, Hassan District.
At that time a Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3170 came in rash and negligent manner and has dashed against him.
Due to the impact of a accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

14. The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
15. By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents in total on his behalf.
Further, PW.1 has got marked 11 documents on his behalf as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.

Further,
petitioner got examined doctor as PW.2, who has issued disability certificate to him and got marked three documents through the said PW.2 as per Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.
In his chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offender vehicle.
16. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the seizer mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P7 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.

17 . The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and Sriram .B.V vs Prakash .K.K on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141727136/
3 negligent driving of the respondent offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3170.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by him.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
(i) The age and applicable multiplier:- The petitioner has contended in his petition that, as on the date of accident he was aged about 46 years.
The material pertaining to Cr.No.315/21 and other medical documents contemplated as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 46 years.
In addition to that, the petitioner has placed his reliance on the copy of aadhar card.
The said aadhar card reflected the date of birth of petitioner as 01.01.1976.
The accident has occurred on 06.12.2021.
Upon computing the age of the petitioner based on all these materials, it clearly shows that, the petitioner is aged of 45 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
As per the documentary evidence available on record, the age of the petitioner is considered as 45 years as on the date of the accident.

Applying the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298,
the multiplier of 14 is applicable to the present content.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the multiplier of 14 is considered to determine the claim made herein.
(ii) The occupation of petitioner and quantum of income:- The petitioner has contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove the said income.

Hence, in the absence of Sriram .B.V vs Prakash .K.K on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141727136/
4 express proof, it is necessary to determine the income of the petitioner based on the principles of notional income.
The Karnataka State Legal Service Authority has fixed a chart for notional income.
By placing reliance on the said income slab.
The income of the petitioner is to be determined.
As per the said chart the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month as operated to the year 2021.
The annual income of the petitioner shall arrive at Rs.1,80,000/- (Rs.15,000 X 12)

(iii) Nature of injury and percentage of disability:- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner he has examined one doctor Mahesh.V., Orthopedic Surgeon, Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon, Punya Hospital, Channarayapatna, is examined as PW.2 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.14.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained Pelvic fracture.
This witness has opined that, petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability for right lower limb 39.33% and to the whole body at 13%.
The injuries are permanent in nature.
Petitioner has contended that, he is a agriculturist and assessed disability causes effect on the avocation of petitioner.
Hence, the disability is considered at 13%.
The said extent of disability is considerable to determine the compensation under this head.
Annual income X Multiplier X permanent physical disability = Loss of earning capacity.
Thereby the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,27,600/- towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a agriculturist and contended that, he used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.500/-.
As per the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient for 5 days and after discharge from the hospital there must be necessary to take bed rest for at least 25 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.30,000/- (30 days X 500 = Rs.15,000 + 15,000).
(B) Medical and future medical expenditure:-
The petitioner contended that, he has incurred Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and nursing care expenses.
The petitioner has placed his reliance on medical bills.
On perusal of the same it is arrived at Rs.16,200/- as per Ex.P.11.
Further the petitioner has claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
The x-ray shows that the petitioner required further medical expenses of Rs.25,000/-.
By considering the medical and future medical expenditure, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.41,200/- (Rs.16,200/- + Rs.25,000) under this head.

Sriram .B.V vs Prakash .K.K on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141727136/
5
(c) Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 5 days with extended follow up treatment.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance to meet his treatment.

Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries in the accident and has taken assistance of attendant including the assistance of his family members, for which they have suffered loss of income.
This shows that the petitioner has sustained loss towards attendants.
Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injury and attended medication.
This shows that the petitioner has followed the nutrition to meet with his necessary protein and special diet.
By considering all these aspects, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.80,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

19. Non-Pecuniary Loss:- This element of compensation reads as follows;
(a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 45 years as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused him lot of pain to suffer in his future life span.
By considering the nature of the injuries and percentage of disability caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
The available on records reveals that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 45 years as on the date of accident.
This shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of his personal life and amenities of life.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

20. Based on aforesaid considered heads of compensation the tabulations is calculated as below:

6 5

Pain and sufferings Rs. 1,00,000/-
6 Loss of enjoyment and loss Rs. 60,000/-

 Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.6,38,800/- which is just and proper.
21. Admittedly, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
respondent is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,38,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected by me and then pronounced in the open court on this the 5th day of October, 2024).
(Gayathri S Kate) XVIII ADDL.JUDGE & ACJM Court of Small Causes Bengaluru.
